title: Ndutu and the Calving Season
excerpt: From roughly January to March, hundreds of thousands of wildebeest calves are born on the short-grass plains around Ndutu. What it is like to be there.
body:
Ndutu lies on the border of the southern Serengeti and the Ngorongoro Conservation Area. In the early months of the year, it is the centre of the wildlife world.

## The calving season

Around January to March, the migration herds gather on the nutrient-rich short-grass plains. Within a few weeks, a very large number of calves is born, often around February. Calves can stand and run within minutes of birth.

## Predators

So much new life attracts predators. Lions, cheetahs, hyenas and jackals are very active. This is one of the best times to see hunts.

## Off-road driving

Because Ndutu lies partly in the Ngorongoro Conservation Area, off-road driving has historically been allowed in parts of the area, within the rules. Rules can change, and responsible guides keep their distance.

## The lakes

Lake Ndutu and Lake Masek attract flamingos and other water birds. Elephants and giraffes live in the acacia woodland around the lakes.

## Weather

This is in the short dry spell between the short and long rains. Afternoon showers can occur, and the plains are green.

## Where to stay

Seasonal mobile camps move to the area for the calving season. See [what is a mobile camp](/blog/what-is-a-mobile-camp/).

Read our [Ndutu page](/national-parks/ndutu/) or [plan your calving season safari](/travel-proposal/).
